DHCPDynamic Host Configuration ProtocolHands out IP addresses, masks, gateways, and DNS servers automatically (UDP 67 and 68).
DICOMDigital Imaging and Communications in MedicineThe standard for medical image files and their network exchange, by convention on port 104.
DISSDiameter Index Safety SystemGas-specific threaded fittings that make it impossible to connect the wrong gas hose.
dLDeciliterOne tenth of a liter; lab values such as glucose in mg per dL.
DMCADigital Millennium Copyright ActThe 1998 copyright law that bans circumventing digital protections.
DMMDigital multimeterThe handheld meter for voltage, current, resistance, and continuity.
DNADeoxyribonucleic acidThe genetic material; sterilization kills microbes by destroying it.
DNSDomain Name SystemTranslates names such as www.example.com into IP addresses (UDP 53, TCP 53 for zone transfers).
DNVDNV HealthcareAn accrediting organization that surveys hospitals annually under its NIAHO program.
DOTDepartment of TransportationThe US agency whose rules govern compressed gas cylinders.
DVMDigital voltmeterA meter for voltage; in practice the same instrument as a DMM.
ECGElectrocardiogramThe recording of the heart's electrical activity: P wave, QRS complex, T wave.
ECRIECRI InstituteThe independent organization that tests devices and publishes hazard alerts and the annual top-ten hazards list.
EDIElectronic data interchangeStandardized electronic exchange of business documents such as claims and payments.
EEGElectroencephalogramThe recording of the brain's electrical activity from scalp electrodes, in microvolts.
EHRElectronic health recordThe patient's longitudinal digital record, shared across providers.
EMElectromagneticElectric and magnetic fields; EM interference disrupts monitors and telemetry.
EMGElectromyogramThe recording of muscle electrical activity.
EMIElectromagnetic interferenceNoise from motors, power lines, fluorescent lights, and radios that corrupts signals on copper cable.
EMRElectronic medical recordThe hospital's clinical record system: orders, notes, results, medications.
EQAAMI EQ seriesAAMI's equipment management standards: EQ56, EQ89, EQ93, EQ103.
EQ103ANSI/AAMI EQ103Guidance for alternative equipment maintenance programs.
EQ56ANSI/AAMI EQ56The recommended practice for a medical equipment management program.
EQ89ANSI/AAMI EQ89Guidance for scheduled maintenance and performance verification.
EQ93ANSI/AAMI EQ93The vocabulary of medical equipment management.
ESDElectrostatic dischargeStatic electricity that can destroy chips; prevented with a wrist strap, mat, and antistatic bags.
ESUElectrosurgical unitThe generator that cuts and coagulates tissue with high-frequency current above about 100 kHz.
EtCO2End-tidal carbon dioxideThe CO2 concentration at the end of exhalation, normally 35 to 45 mmHg, measured by capnography.
ETOEthylene oxideA toxic gas used to sterilize heat-sensitive devices.
FDAFood and Drug AdministrationThe US regulator of medical devices; classes I to III, recalls, and medical device reporting.
FDGFluorodeoxyglucoseThe glucose-like radioactive tracer used in PET scans.
FEV1Forced expiratory volume in one secondThe volume exhaled in the first second of a forced breath out.
FHIRFast Healthcare Interoperability ResourcesHL7's web-style standard using REST APIs and JSON resources.
FHRFetal heart rateThe baby's heart rate, measured by ultrasound Doppler on a fetal monitor.
FiO2Fraction of inspired oxygenThe oxygen concentration being delivered, from 0.21 (room air) to 1.0.
FSHFollicle-stimulating hormoneThe pituitary hormone that drives sperm production and egg development.
FVCForced vital capacityThe total volume a patient can exhale forcefully after a full breath in.
GbpsGigabits per secondBillions of bits per second; gigabit Ethernet is 1 Gbps.
GFCIGround-fault circuit interrupterA receptacle or breaker that trips when current leaking to ground exceeds about 5 mA.
GHSGlobally Harmonized SystemThe international standard for chemical hazard labels and safety data sheets.
GHzGigahertzBillions of cycles per second; CPU clock speed and Wi-Fi band frequency.
GIGastrointestinalThe digestive tract.
H2OWaterThe pressure unit centimeters of water (cmH2O) for airway and ventilator pressures.
HDDHard disk driveSpinning magnetic storage: cheap per terabyte, slower, and fragile.
HFAPHealthcare Facilities Accreditation ProgramThe former osteopathic hospital accreditation program, now part of ACHC.
HHSDepartment of Health and Human ServicesThe US department that enforces HIPAA through its Office for Civil Rights.
HIPAAHealth Insurance Portability and Accountability ActThe US law protecting health information; Title II holds the privacy and security rules.
HITECHHealth Information Technology for Economic and Clinical Health ActThe 2009 law that funded EHR adoption and strengthened HIPAA enforcement and breach notification.
HITRUSTHealth Information Trust AllianceA certifiable security framework that combines HIPAA, NIST, and other requirements for healthcare.
HIVHuman immunodeficiency virusA bloodborne virus; one of the pathogens the OSHA bloodborne pathogen standard addresses.
HLHearing levelThe decibel scale audiometers use, referenced to normal hearing thresholds.
HL7Health Level SevenThe messaging standard that connects clinical systems: version 2 pipes, version 3 XML, FHIR web APIs.
HRHeart rateBeats per minute, derived from the ECG or pulse.
HTTPHypertext Transfer ProtocolWeb traffic in the clear on TCP 80.
HTTPSHypertext Transfer Protocol SecureHTTP inside TLS on TCP 443.
HVHigh voltageThe kilovolt sections of X-ray generators, defibrillators, and ESUs.
HVACHeating, ventilation, and air conditioningThe building's climate systems, which keep server rooms cool and are themselves networked controls.
HzHertzCycles per second; display refresh rate, AC mains frequency, and signal frequency.
IaaSInfrastructure as a serviceThe provider supplies virtual machines, storage, and networks; you manage the operating system and up.
IABPIntra-aortic balloon pumpA balloon in the aorta that inflates in diastole and deflates in systole to support the heart.
IARCInternational Agency for Research on CancerThe WHO body that classifies carcinogens.
IBPInvasive blood pressurePressure measured directly through an arterial line and a transducer.
ICIntegrated circuitA chip: many transistors on one piece of silicon.
ICMPInternet Control Message ProtocolThe protocol behind ping and traceroute.
ICUIntensive care unitThe critical care area with the highest density of monitors, ventilators, and pumps.
IDIdentificationA patient identifier or a device identifier.
IECInternational Electrotechnical CommissionThe international standards body; IEC 60601-1 is the medical electrical equipment safety standard.
IEEEInstitute of Electrical and Electronics EngineersThe engineering body behind Ethernet (802.3), Wi-Fi (802.11), and many device standards.
IPInternet ProtocolThe Layer 3 protocol that addresses and routes packets between networks.
IPv4Internet Protocol version 432-bit addresses written as four decimal octets, such as 192.168.1.10.
IPv6Internet Protocol version 6128-bit addresses in eight hex groups; no broadcast, built-in autoconfiguration.
ISOInternational Organization for Standardization; also an ISO disc imageThe standards body, and the .iso file format that holds a complete disc image.
ITInformation technologyComputers, networks, and the people who run them.
IUPCIntrauterine pressure catheterA catheter that measures contraction pressure directly.
IVIntravenousInto a vein; IV lines, pumps, and fluids.
KCLKirchhoff's current lawCurrent into a node equals current out.
kHzKilohertzOne thousand cycles per second.
kVKilovoltOne thousand volts; X-ray tube voltage and defibrillator charge levels.
KVLKirchhoff's voltage lawThe voltages around any closed loop sum to zero.
KVMKeyboard, video, mouse (switch)One keyboard, monitor, and mouse shared among several computers.
KVOKeep vein openA very low infusion rate that keeps an IV line from clotting.
kWKilowattOne thousand watts of power.
kWhKilowatt-hourThe energy unit on the electric bill: one kilowatt for one hour.
LALeft arm electrode (also left atrium)The black ECG electrode on the left arm; in heart anatomy, the left atrium.
LANLocal area networkOne site's network: a building, floor, or campus that one organization owns and runs.
LC50Lethal concentration 50 percentThe airborne concentration lethal to half of test subjects.
LCDLiquid crystal displayThe flat panel that shapes light from a backlight into an image; TN, IPS, and VA are the panel types.
LD50Lethal dose 50 percentThe dose that kills half of test subjects.
LEDLight-emitting diodeA small light source: the status lights on a port, the lamp in cheap fiber transmitters, and modern display backlights.
LHLuteinizing hormoneThe pituitary hormone that drives testosterone and triggers ovulation.
LIMLine isolation monitorContinuously measures how much current a fault could drive from an isolated power system to ground and alarms at 5 mA.
LIMSLaboratory information management systemSample and workflow tracking software for laboratories.
LISLaboratory information systemThe software that manages lab orders, analyzer results, and reporting.
LLLeft leg electrodeThe red ECG electrode on the left leg.
LVLeft ventricleThe chamber that pumps blood to the body at systemic pressure.
LVPLarge-volume pumpAn infusion pump for bags of fluid, usually peristaltic, accurate to about 5 percent.
mAMilliampereOne thousandth of an ampere; the unit for shock thresholds and leakage currents.
MACMedia access control (address)The 48-bit hardware address burned into a network interface, used at Layer 2.
MAPMean arterial pressureThe average arterial pressure: diastolic plus one third of the pulse pressure.
MDDSMedical device data systemSoftware or hardware that transfers, stores, or displays device data without changing it.
MDS2Manufacturer Disclosure Statement for Medical Device SecurityThe standard form describing a device's security capabilities.
MFAMulti-factor authenticationTwo or more different kinds of proof of identity.
MHzMegahertzMillions of cycles per second; memory speed, radio channels, and older CPU clocks.
mLMilliliterOne thousandth of a liter; tidal volumes, drug doses, and infusion rates in mL per hour.
mmHgMillimeters of mercuryThe pressure unit for blood pressure, gas pressures, and vacuum.
MRMagnetic resonanceThe MRI environment; equipment is labeled MR Safe, MR Conditional, or MR Unsafe.
MRIMagnetic resonance imagingImaging with a strong magnet and radio pulses; no ionizing radiation, but the magnet is always on.
MRNMedical record numberThe hospital's unique identifier for a patient.
msMillisecondOne thousandth of a second; latency, pulse widths, and ECG timing.
MSHMessage header segmentThe first segment of every HL7 version 2 message.
mVMillivoltOne thousandth of a volt; ECG signals are about 1 mV.
NATNetwork address translationRewrites private inside addresses to a public address at the router so many hosts can share it.
NECNational Electrical CodeThe US wiring code, NFPA 70.
NESCNational Electrical Safety CodeThe utility-side safety code for power lines and substations.
NFPANational Fire Protection AssociationThe standards body for fire and electrical safety: NFPA 70 (NEC), NFPA 99 (health care facilities), NFPA 101 (life safety).
NIAHONational Integrated Accreditation for Healthcare OrganizationsDNV's hospital accreditation program.
NIBPNon-invasive blood pressureAutomatic cuff measurement by the oscillometric method.
NIOSHNational Institute for Occupational Safety and HealthThe CDC's research arm for workplace safety, which publishes RELs.
NISTNational Institute of Standards and TechnologyThe US standards body whose cybersecurity framework hospitals use.
NPNNegative-positive-negative transistorA bipolar transistor that conducts when its base is pulled positive.
NPSGNational Patient Safety GoalsThe Joint Commission's annual list of safety priorities, including alarm management.
NTCNegative temperature coefficient (thermistor)A thermistor whose resistance falls as temperature rises; the sensor in patient temperature probes.
NTPNational Toxicology ProgramThe US program that publishes the Report on Carcinogens, one of the carcinogen listings cited on a safety data sheet.
NTPNetwork Time ProtocolThe protocol (UDP 123) that keeps device clocks synchronized so logs, alarms, and records line up.
OBRObservation request segmentThe HL7 segment describing the order a result answers.
OBXObservation segmentThe HL7 segment holding one observation and its value.
OCROffice for Civil RightsThe HHS office that enforces HIPAA privacy and security rules.
OROperating roomThe surgical suite, with isolated power, ESUs, anesthesia machines, and lasers.
ORMOrder messageThe HL7 version 2 message that carries an order.
ORUObservation resultThe HL7 message that carries results, including vital signs from monitors.
OSHAOccupational Safety and Health AdministrationThe US agency that sets workplace safety rules.
OSIOpen Systems Interconnection modelThe seven-layer model for describing where a network function happens.
OXOxidizer (NFPA 704 symbol)The special hazard code in the white diamond for oxidizing materials.
PaaSPlatform as a serviceThe provider runs the platform (OS, runtime, database); you deploy code.
PACSPicture archiving and communication systemThe server that stores and distributes medical images using DICOM.
PASSPull, aim, squeeze, sweepHow to use a fire extinguisher.
PCPersonal computerA desktop or laptop for one user.
PCAPatient-controlled analgesiaAn infusion pump that lets the patient self-dose pain medication within programmed limits.
PCBPrinted circuit boardThe board that holds and connects a device's components.
PDCAPlan, do, check, actThe continuous improvement cycle.
PEEPPositive end-expiratory pressurePressure the ventilator keeps in the lungs at the end of exhalation so alveoli stay open.
PELPermissible exposure limitOSHA's legal maximum exposure to a substance, averaged over a shift.
PETPositron emission tomographyNuclear imaging of metabolic activity using a positron-emitting tracer such as FDG.
pHPotential of hydrogenThe acidity scale; blood is normally 7.35 to 7.45.
PHIProtected health informationAny health information tied to an identifiable person.
PIDPatient identification segmentThe HL7 segment carrying patient name, ID, and demographics.
PMPreventive maintenanceScheduled inspection and testing of equipment before it fails.
PNPPositive-negative-positive transistorA bipolar transistor that conducts when its base is pulled negative.
PoEPower over EthernetDelivers DC power to devices over the data cable: 802.3af 15.4 W, 802.3at 30 W, 802.3bt 60 to 90 W.
PPPulse pressureSystolic minus diastolic pressure.
PPEPersonal protective equipmentGloves, gowns, masks, eye protection, and lead aprons.
PPPPoint-to-Point ProtocolThe Layer 2 protocol for serial and dial-up links that carries IP with authentication.
PRPR intervalThe ECG interval from the start of the P wave to the start of the QRS, 0.12 to 0.20 seconds; the AV node delay.
psiPounds per square inchThe pressure unit for cylinders, sterilizers, and pneumatic systems.
PSUPower supply unitConverts wall AC to the DC voltages a computer needs: 12 V, 5 V, 3.3 V.
PSVPressure support ventilationThe ventilator boosts each spontaneous breath with a set pressure.
PTPhysical therapyThe rehabilitation department, whose equipment includes TENS units, stimulators, and therapeutic ultrasound.
QCQuality controlRunning known samples to verify an analyzer is reading correctly.
QRSQRS complexThe sharp ECG spike of ventricular depolarization; normally under 0.12 seconds wide.
QTQT intervalThe ECG interval from the start of the QRS to the end of the T wave, under about 0.44 seconds.
RARight arm electrode (also right atrium)The white ECG electrode on the right arm; in heart anatomy, the right atrium.
RACERescue, alarm, confine, extinguish or evacuateThe order of actions when a fire is discovered.
RADIUSRemote Authentication Dial-In User ServiceThe AAA server behind Wi-Fi Enterprise, VPNs, and 802.1X; UDP 1812 and 1813.
RAIDRedundant array of independent disksCombining disks for speed, capacity, or fault tolerance: 0 stripe, 1 mirror, 5 stripe with parity, 6 double parity, 10 mirrored stripes.
RAMRandom-access memoryThe working memory that holds running programs and data; lost at power off.
RCResistor-capacitor (circuit)A resistor and capacitor together, whose time constant is R times C.
RCARoot cause analysisA structured investigation of what happened, why, and how to prevent it.
RCFRelative centrifugal forceThe g-force a centrifuge applies, which depends on speed and rotor radius.
RELRecommended exposure limitNIOSH's recommended exposure limit.
REMRoentgen equivalent manA unit of radiation dose equivalent, 100 rem equals 1 sievert.
RFRadio frequencyRadio signals; the medium of Wi-Fi, cellular, and Bluetooth, and a source of interference and, in medicine, surgical energy.
RISRadiology information systemScheduling, tracking, and reporting for imaging departments.
RJ45Registered jack 45The eight-pin plug on Ethernet twisted-pair cables (properly an 8P8C connector).
RLRight leg electrodeThe green ECG electrode on the right leg, the reference or driven ground.
RMSRoot mean squareThe effective value of an AC voltage or current, the DC equivalent for heating; 120 V mains is RMS.
RPMRevolutions per minuteRotation speed: hard drive platters at 5400 or 7200, fans, and laboratory centrifuges.
RS-232Recommended Standard 232 serialThe classic serial port: slow, simple, and still used for console access and legacy devices.
RTLSReal-time location systemTags and receivers that track equipment location inside the hospital.
RVRight ventricleThe chamber that pumps blood to the lungs.
SASinoatrial nodeThe heart's natural pacemaker in the right atrium.
SaaSSoftware as a serviceComplete applications delivered over the web, such as email and office suites.
SATSource address tableThe switch's table of which MAC address lives on which port.
SBOMSoftware bill of materialsA list of the software components inside a device.
SBPSystolic blood pressureThe peak arterial pressure during ventricular contraction.
SCDSequential compression deviceInflatable leg sleeves that inflate in sequence to prevent blood clots.
SCRSilicon-controlled rectifierA thyristor that switches large currents on when triggered and stays on until current stops.
SDSSafety data sheetThe document describing a chemical's hazards, handling, and first aid.
SIMVSynchronized intermittent mandatory ventilationA ventilator mode that gives a set number of breaths synchronized with the patient's own efforts.
SMARTSelf-Monitoring, Analysis, and Reporting TechnologyHard drive self-diagnostics that warn before failure.
SMBServer Message BlockWindows file and printer sharing on TCP 445.
SMDASafe Medical Devices ActThe 1990 law requiring hospitals to report device-related deaths and serious injuries to the FDA and manufacturer.
SMPSSwitch-mode power supplyA power supply that switches at high frequency to regulate voltage efficiently.
SpO2Peripheral oxygen saturationThe percentage of hemoglobin carrying oxygen, measured by a pulse oximeter.
SSDSolid-state driveFlash storage with no moving parts: fast, silent, and shock resistant.
SSHSecure ShellEncrypted remote command-line access and file transfer on TCP 22; replaces Telnet and FTP.
STST segmentThe ECG segment between the QRS and the T wave, where injury and ischemia show as elevation or depression.
STELShort-term exposure limitThe maximum average exposure over a 15-minute period.
SVTSupraventricular tachycardiaA fast, regular rhythm originating above the ventricles, with narrow QRS.
TCTransport CanadaThe Canadian counterpart of the DOT for cylinder rules.
TCPTransmission Control ProtocolReliable, ordered, connection-based transport: three-way handshake, acknowledgments, retransmission.
TDRTime-domain reflectometerA cable tester that finds the distance to a break from signal reflections.
TENSTranscutaneous electrical nerve stimulationLow-level electrical pulses through skin electrodes for pain relief.
TLSTransport Layer SecurityThe encryption layer under HTTPS and most secure protocols; use 1.2 or 1.3.
TLVThreshold limit valueThe ACGIH recommended exposure limit.
TOCOTocodynamometerThe pressure sensor on a fetal monitor that records uterine contractions.
TPNTotal parenteral nutritionComplete nutrition delivered into a vein through an infusion pump.
TRTelecommunications roomThe wiring closet on each floor that serves nearby devices within the 90 m horizontal cable limit.
TVTelevisionA display or broadcast receiver; smart TVs are IoT devices.
UDPUser Datagram ProtocolConnectionless, fast transport with no delivery guarantee; used for voice, video, DNS, DHCP.
UEFIUnified Extensible Firmware InterfaceModern firmware that replaces BIOS: GPT disks, Secure Boot, mouse-driven setup.
UNUnited NationsThe body whose Globally Harmonized System is the format hazard communication now uses.
UPSUninterruptible power supplyA battery unit that keeps equipment running through a power cut and conditions the power.
USUnited StatesThe country; used for US standards, the 60 Hz mains frequency, and the AHA electrode color code.
USBUniversal Serial BusThe standard port for peripherals, storage, and charging.
uVMicrovoltOne millionth of a volt; EEG signals are in microvolts.
UVUltravioletLight beyond violet, used for disinfection and in spectrophotometers, and absorbed by glass and plastic.
VAVolt-ampereThe unit of apparent power, which a supply must deliver regardless of power factor.
VARVolt-ampere reactiveThe unit of reactive power, which shuttles between source and load without doing work.
VFVentricular fibrillationChaotic ventricular activity with no output; the rhythm defibrillators treat.
VLANVirtual local area networkA logical LAN on a switch: ports in different VLANs are separate broadcast domains.
VMVirtual machineA complete computer running as software on a hypervisor.
VPNVirtual private networkAn encrypted tunnel across an untrusted network such as the internet.
VTVentricular tachycardiaA fast rhythm from the ventricles with wide QRS complexes; pulseless VT is shockable.
VTTidal volumeThe volume of one breath, set on a ventilator at about 6 to 8 mL per kilogram of ideal body weight.
WANWide area networkConnects LANs across cities or countries, usually over links leased from a provider.
WEPWired Equivalent PrivacyThe original Wi-Fi encryption, broken in minutes; never use it.
Wi-FiWireless fidelityThe trade name for IEEE 802.11 wireless networking.
WIPOWorld Intellectual Property OrganizationThe UN agency for international copyright and patent treaties.
WLANWireless local area networkA LAN delivered over Wi-Fi instead of cables.
WMTSWireless Medical Telemetry ServiceThe FCC-protected bands for patient telemetry: 608 to 614, 1395 to 1400, and 1427 to 1432 MHz.
WPA2Wi-Fi Protected Access 2Wi-Fi security using AES with CCMP; still common and acceptable.
WPA3Wi-Fi Protected Access 3The current Wi-Fi security standard: SAE in Personal mode, stronger encryption, protected management frames.
XMLExtensible Markup LanguageA text format for structured data; HL7 version 3 and CDA use it.
YAGYttrium aluminum garnet (laser)The crystal in Nd:YAG lasers, which emit near-infrared light that penetrates tissue.
YSIYellow Springs Instruments (temperature probe standard)The company whose YSI 400 and YSI 700 thermistor curves became the standards for temperature probes.
